speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether vaccinations for COVID-19 will be incorporated into the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule; and (b) if so, whether parents will have a choice between mRNA and non-mRNA vaccines.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the current COVID-19 Omicron wave (a) whether the hospitalisation rate of 1.9% is expected to rise as more restrictions are removed; (b) what is the highest hospitalisation rate that our public hospitals can currently accommodate; and (c) whether the Government will look into mandating targeted vaccines against the Omicron variant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am very thankful that the number of questions on COVID-19 has decreased significantly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about COVID-19 hospitalisation rates that our public hospitals can accommodate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, what we need to do is to continue to keep our vaccinations "up to date", prevent ourselves from falling severely ill if we are infected, we must exercise social responsibility, such as staying at home and self-testing when not feeling well, and do whatever we can to optimise our hospital capacity.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have been and will continue to re-allocate our healthcare resources on a dynamic basis to where they are needed most.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked about vaccines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are bringing in bivalent vaccines into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is provided for in our agreements with the pharmaceutical companies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The bivalent vaccines will target both the ancestral strain of COVID-19 and the Omicron variant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our intention is to update our vaccines for the National Vaccination Programme as the formulations improve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will share more details when the arrangements are confirmed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Nevertheless, existing vaccines remain highly protective against severe disease, including for the Omicron BA.5 variant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you are eligible to receive another vaccine dose, please receive your vaccination without delay and not wait for variant-specific vaccines, as COVID-19 is still spreading in the community.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will now turn to the Member’s question about COVID-19 in children.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member also asked about children’s vaccinations for COVID-19, such as whether Novavax will be made available for those aged 18 and below and whether the vaccines have long-term effects on children.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Currently, HSA as well as the Expert Committee on COVID-19 Vaccination (EC19V) are independently evaluating the Novavax vaccine for young persons aged 12 to 17.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Novavax has not submitted the application for its vaccine to be administered to children under 12.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about vaccination-differentiated measures.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the height of an infection wave, measures are taken to prevent our healthcare system from being overwhelmed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, when cases are lower and steady, many of these measures, including mask-wearing, for example, have been removed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Others, such as vaccinations and vaccination-differentiated safe management measures (VDS), are kept in some form, in anticipation of another infection wave.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is the nature of crisis management – we stand down many measures when they are not needed but we need to keep some, in anticipation of something worse happening later.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While VDS is mandated for specific settings, such as events with more than 500 participants at any one time, business owners and employers also have the flexibility to implement conditions of service that are relevant to their settings, such as requiring the donning of masks, as well as adopting vaccination-related instructions for customers or for workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Nevertheless, as the Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) had explained in previous replies, we are reviewing vaccination requirements, from one of counting number of doses and boosters we are taking, to ensuring that our vaccination is "up to date".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will be a more enduring posture as we live with COVID-19 as an endemic disease.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We expect to complete this review in the next couple of months and will review VDS at the same time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note the Minister's response on adding COVID-19 vaccinations into the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It will give assurance to parents that the COVID-19 vaccination does play an important role to better protect children against severe complications, such as Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in children.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What else is the Ministry doing to encourage more parents to vaccinate their children for COVID-19?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My second supplementary question is when will MOH allow children below the age of five to get the COVID-19 vaccination, since other countries, such as the US, have allowed COVID-19 vaccines for babies aged six months to toddlers aged four years?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the second question first, children under five, we have the supplies; it is part of our supply agreement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Details will be announced once we are ready.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, it is through encouraging parents through transparent information that we hope more parents will bring their children to get vaccinated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I ask, in part, because I believe many of us still have residents that – for religious, health or personal reasons – have chosen not to be vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think it is difficult to adopt a blanket policy to say all in the public sector shall not insist on VDS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For each setting, it depends on whether it is crowded, whether seniors are present in those settings, what is the risk of transmission.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we always need to take a differentiated approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We must remember that as we increasingly treat COVID-19 as endemic, "endemic" does not mean that it is not there.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Endemic means to acknowledge that it is there and we have to adjust to our normal life and normal procedures in order to live with the virus.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And one of the principles to do so is to make sure that, according to the risk of different settings, we adopt the necessary measures to manage the risks.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, it is in this spirit that we allow employers and building owners to impose their own VDS requirements should they need to.
